title: Unattended posture: a read-only run that finishes with no operator, contained by something that is not a word list

AC1.note: unattended.test.ts 'AC1: a scripted read-only run answers a real project question with human_interventions: 0' — reads 7.3.1 off disk, answers from the tool result, counter 0, stamped into the record. LIMIT, from the review and not hidden: on a host whose global keryx predates 377fc325, search_code returns a skew diagnosis instead of results, so 14 of 15 tools work and this criterion is degraded in exactly the CI case the flow targets. Documented as soft edge 3 in harness.md and cli-reference.md

AC2.note: unattended-corpus.test.ts 'AC2/C-1': 16 commands x every profile, real git init, tree hash + graph index + package.json byte-compared, .env marker absent from output/history/stream. Independent reviewer re-ran a 60+ attempt escape harness against the same tree: zero leaks, filesystem unchanged

AC3.note: unattended-corpus.test.ts 'AC3/C-2': all 52 grant patterns, verdict recorded per line, every one refused-at-launch. The flag grammar has no slot a grant can bind to

AC4.note: unattended-corpus.test.ts 'AC4/C-3' (11 shell-borne escapes) and the read-tool-equivalent pair contained by root confinement. Reviewer re-ran independently: refused

AC5.note: unattended-corpus.test.ts 'AC5/C-4' end to end against real ripgrep incl. the symlink; plus search-code-confinement.test.ts, whose vacuous half was found by review and split into MUST_BUILD (15 inputs that produce argv, shape invariants claimed there) and a counted refusal test over the 19 escape inputs. New search-code-real-chain.test.ts exercises search_code -> keryx ctx rg -> rg with no injected runner

AC6.note: Four unit/driven tests plus a real-binary CLI spawn. Reviewer ran both surfaces of the actual binary: full stdout diff is three lines (header segment, session id, tool list), and summary.json carries neither posture nor humanInterventions on the supervised path. Byte-identical approval prompt and header pinned by approvalPromptLine/shellHeaderSubtitle

AC7.note: unattended.test.ts: an ask with no approver resolves to deny with and without the posture; a deny stays terminal — an approver returning true cannot run a tool the posture denies (real tool smuggled past the array filter, refused at the invocation seam, approver never asked)

AC8.note: Ten guards, each reverted and re-run by an INDEPENDENT reviewer, not by the implementer: eligibility risk 7 failures, requiresApprover 4, executeCall seam 1 (right mechanism), installed approver 1, forced --no-follow 4 (shape only, stated as such), --regexp= operand 4 (shape only), confineToRoot realpath 7, makeKeryxRunner env 2, deny-list --follow 4, skew rule 1. Two guards were pinned by NOTHING in the first round (installed approver: 0 failures across all 3173 tests) and one only incidentally (realpath: 2, both search_code, while an SSH key leaked unnoticed); both fixed and re-verified

AC9.note: harness.md now carries four soft edges: not a secrecy boundary (read_file/search_code read anything inside the root incl. .env), the two lists surviving in search_code named as lists that will be incomplete, the walk/operand split (--no-follow guards the tree walk; a symlink named AS the operand is followed, and only realpath stops it — measured against rg 14.1.1), and the PATH-version dependency. Reviewer found no sentence asserting a category guarantee the mechanism implements as a list

AC10.note: Refusal properties, not table entries: shell_exec was never constructed for the array (no code parsed a command); a tool's own declared risk class, undeclared failing closed; the tool's own requiresApprover; an approver that takes nothing it could weigh; the flag grammar having no slot a grant can occupy; realpath containment for paths; --regexp= inline with exactly one confined operand so no operand meaning can shift. The one surviving list is a PERMIT list on forwarded rg options, which can only be too narrow, and the docs say so

AC11.note: unattended.test.ts x3 plus a real-binary run: header shows unattended:read-only, the record carries posture and humanInterventions 0, and it survives being read back on resume. The stamp is written at session open, not after a successful turn — a defect the CLI spawn test found and unit tests would not have

AC12.note: Independently re-run by me on the fix commit: bun run check 3168 pass, 14 skip, 0 fail, exit 0 (3182 tests, 312 files); check:doc-links 650 links across 203 files, 0 broken. The 14 skips are pre-existing environment gates (real-subprocess, macOS sandbox, PTY, OpenTUI); none added, none weakened
